_comment: Curated crown-group / divergence ages (Ma) for key nodes, keyed by OTT id. Each entry is one published estimate with its citation. kind: 'clock' = molecular-clock estimate (min_ma/max_ma = reported interval), 'fossil_minimum' = oldest accepted fossil of the crown group (a minimum age, not the divergence itself), 'biomarker' = biomarker evidence. No TimeTree values are used anywhere. check='secondary' means the value was restated from the paper's abstract or a review summary and has not been re-checked against the full text for this release.

304358.note: Bangiomorpha pubescens, a crown-group red alga, so a minimum for crown Eukaryota.
Crown-group eukaryote steroids become abundant only from the Tonian (~800 Ma); stem-group protosterol biota from ~1600 Ma.

691846.note: Crown Metazoa; the authors stress that current data cannot narrow this interval much.

117569.note: Ikaria wariootia, 2-7 mm, Ediacara Member, South Australia; oldest bilaterian body fossil.

611099.note: Saccorhytus (Fortunian, ~535 Ma) reinterpreted as an early ecdysozoan.

632179.note: Oldest trilobite body fossils (~521 Ma); arthropod trace fossils are older.

1048707.note: Crown Pterygota (winged insects), Early Devonian; oldest winged-insect fossils are ~325 Ma.

150772.note: Mites in the Rhynie chert (Early Devonian), among the oldest terrestrial animals.

391142.note: Origin of volvocine multicellularity (Triassic, ~200 Ma). Strictly this dates the stem of the colonial volvocine clade, which is older than crown Volvocaceae.

56610.note: Crown embryophytes (land plants), mid-Cambrian to Early Ordovician.
